The difference of squares formula is given by a2−b2=(a+b)(a−b)

Notice that our expression can be written as a difference of squares: t4−16=(t2)2−42

Now, we factor our expression using the difference of squares formula: (t2)2−42=(t2+4)(t2−4)

Finally, we notice that the expression in the second set of parentheses is also a difference of squares. Therefore, the expression can be factored further, as follows: (t2+4)(t2−4)=(t2+4)(t2−22)=(t2+4)(t+2)(t−2)

3.?

Factor the expression 3x42−24.

M
Wed, Jul 15th @ 8:49 PM|Elapsed: 1:01Correct

The difference of squares formula is given by

a2−b2=(a+b)(a−b)

Notice that x4 has a factor of 32. To simplify the computation, we can factor out the 32 in our expression, as follows:

3x42−24=32⋅x4−32⋅16=32(x4−16)

The expression in parentheses can be written as a difference of squares: 32(x4−16)=32((x2)2−42)

Now, we factor our expression using the difference of squares formula: 32((x2)2−42)=32(x2+4)(x2−4)

Finally, we notice that the expression in the second set of parentheses is also a difference of squares. Therefore, the expression can be factored further, as follows: 32(x2+4)(x2−4)=32(x2+4)(x2−22)=32(x2+4)(x+2)(x−2)

4.?

Wed, Jul 15th @ 8:50 PM|Elapsed: 0:55Correct

a2−b2=(a+b)(a−b)

Notice that all of the terms in our expression have a common factor of 3. To simplify the computation, we can factor out the 3, as follows:

3x4−48=3⋅x4−3⋅16=3(x4−16)

The expression in parentheses can be written as a difference of squares: 3(x4−16)=3((x2)2−42)

Now, we factor our expression using the difference of squares formula: 3((x2)2−42)=3(x2+4)(x2−4)

Finally, we notice that the expression in the second set of parentheses is also a difference of squares. Therefore, the expression can be factored further, as follows: 3(x2+4)(x2−4)=3(x2+4)(x2−22)=3(x2+4)(x+2)(x−2)

Now, we factor our expression using the difference of squares formula: (r2)2−((5s)2)2=(r2+(5s)2)(r2−(5s)2)=(r2+25s2)(r2−(5s)2)
